results.title: How the Right MIS Can Reduce Teacher Workload | Compass Education UK
results.content: # Reduce Teacher Workload in UK Schools: Compass MIS in Action. * **Modern MIS = real time savings:** An integrated MIS like Compass can reduce teacher workload by 30–50%, saving 3–7 hours weekly through automation and streamlined workflows. If you’re searching for ways to **reduce teacher workload**, this data shows it’s possible to reclaim up to 50% of your admin time. According to the Department for Education ‘Exporing teachers’ admin time’ report, teachers and middle leaders spend **an average of 2 hours per day** on administrative tasks. Full-time teachers reported working **an average of 52.4 hours per week**, and for school leaders, it was around **58.2 hours.** On paper, teaching is meant to be a 32.5-hour job, but these figures show just how far reality overshoots what’s written into contracts. When I joined Compass Education as a Client Consultant, I discovered what I’d desperately needed as a teacher: a single, integrated platform that actually understands how schools work and has the potential to reduce teacher workload. > ***“In a survey following our training, 100% of teachers responded that the School Reports process in Compass reduced their workload.”***. Understanding what makes a great School MIS system means recognising how data should work for teachers, not against them. Schools using integrated MIS can **reduce teacher workload by 30-50%** across all administrative areas:. Leaders across a multi-academy trust echoed this sentiment, and shared how Compass is helping them ***“build an integrated, dynamic approach that reduces workload, strengthens community engagement, and supports every aspect of school life.”*** They were quick to credit the dedicated, responsive teams guiding them through development, migration, and technical support, describing it as a partnership that makes them feel supported at every step. Unlike the disconnected systems that added to my teacher workload, Compass MIS was built by educators who understood the daily reality of school life. * **Integrated parent communication** through the Compass Parent App. Explore all the features designed to reduce teacher workload. Drawing on research from the Learning Policy Institute, replacing a departing teacher can cost schools nearly £20,000 when you factor in the time and resources needed for separation, recruitment, hiring, and training.

results.title: CHS under EHR meaningful use investigation | Healthcare Dive
results.content: # CHS under EHR meaningful use investigation. * Community Health Systems is currently under civil investigation over EHR adoption and compliance to government standards that regulate incentive payments under the federal Meaningful Use program. Although it's unclear whether the civil investigative demand was filed by a state attorney general's office or from federal investigators at the Justice Department or Office of Inspector General, CHS indicated it is responding to subpoenas and other demands. * CHS, one of the country's largest for-profit health systems, uses three EHR networks across its 118 hospitals: Cerner, Medhost and an in-house system from Health Management Associates (HMA), a 70-hospital organization CHS acquired in 2014. EHR incentive payments have increasingly found themselves under the microscope of federal investigators in the past year or so. The scrutiny stems in part from the 2017 eClinicalWorks controversy in which the EHR company paid out $155 million to DOJ following whistleblower allegations that it knowingly caused providers to submit fraudulent EHR incentive payments. Through the Meaningful Use program, the government distributed more than $38 billion to providers to install EHR systems. But OIG reported that last year alone federal investigators issued $729 million in inappropriate incentive payments. OIG is currently conducting a second review of Medicare EHR incentive payments, which it plans to publish later this year. According to annual financial filingsanalyzed by Fierce Healthcare, CHS received more than $865 million in EHR incentive payments between 2011 and 2017 through the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act enacted in 2009. According to the filing from CHS, management does "not believe that loss contingencies arising from pending legal, regulatory and governmental matters, including the matters described herein, will have a material adverse effect on the consolidated financial position or liquidity" of the company. Though CHS and Cerner did not respond to a request for comment, Medhost representative Samra Khan said in an email to Healthcare Dive "it is MEDHOST's policy to not make specific comments regarding customer matters.". results.title: What schools can do to reduce teacher workload - Groupcall
results.content: Back to Blog Articles # What schools can do to reduce teacher workload * 41% of teachers say their workload is **unmanageable most or all of the time**, and only about 20% feel it is manageable much of the time. * In Scotland, research shows that many teachers put in **7 or more hours of unpaid overtime per week**, with a quarter working over **15 extra hours**. These figures make clear that the issue is widespread, not isolated to a few schools or regions. * Support for workload accountability (making sure tasks are necessary and not duplicated). * Bring teacher voice into decisions about workload policy: what do staff believe could be cut? ## Discover more articles
